source.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
source.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools to keep the two phases from interfering. In practice, this creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate while decode nodes have compute underutilized, and on a production-style A100 cluster with 2 prefill and 2 decode nodes (2P2D), we find that prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 Time-to-First-Token (TTFT). Queuing and inter-node GPU-GPU KV-cache transfer account for the rest. We present a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler that lets decode nodes serve prefill phase of requests as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with their in-flight decode batches. For each queued request, we estimate the TTFT it would see on the prefill node, and on every decode node, search for the largest chunk schedule that keeps in-flight decodes within their Time-Between-Tokens (TBT) SLO and deflect when the decode path helps tail latency. Because the prefill phase of deflected requests runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM and evaluated on production-style traces with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, our approach reduces P95 TTFT by upto 81% and raises SLO attainment by upto 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers, at sub-millisecond per-request routing cost.

previous_facts.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
previous_facts.event_hint: Kairos: a load-aware prefill-deflection scheduler that runs deflected prefill in place on decode nodes to cut P95 TTFT up to 81% and eliminate inter-node KV-cache transfer in disaggregated LLM serving.
previous_facts.problem: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, which creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate and queue while decode nodes sit underutilized (decode is memory-bound with spare compute). On a 2P2D A100 cluster the authors show prefill execution is only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait and inter-node GPU-to-GPU KV-cache transfer, both scheduling artifacts rather than compute limits. Prior disaggregated designs (Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer) assume a request stays on its prefill node until prefill completes and then ships its KV cache to a decode node, so they cannot exploit the spare compute on decode nodes.
previous_facts.mechanism: Kairos is a proactive, time-aware prefill-deflection scheduler. For each queued request it estimates TTFT on the prefill node from current queue depth/order, and for every decode node sweeps candidate chunk-size sequences using an analytical TBT-safety model that predicts per-step decode latency from in-flight decode batch size, KV-cache occupancy, and added prefill chunk size (no live inference trials; one-time deployment-time profiling; no model changes). It deflects the request's prefill phase to a decode node when both (i) TBT safety holds (in-flight decode step latency stays within the TBT SLO tau, with margin beta) and (ii) projected decode-node TTFT is at most alpha times the prefill-node TTFT, where alpha >= 1 is a single operator-tunable knob (alpha=1 deflects only when the decode path is strictly faster). Deflected prefill runs as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with in-flight decode batches, so the prefill phase executes in place on the decode node and the inter-node KV-cache transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM 0.18.1 (~2000 lines of Python); per-request scheduling overhead is below 1 ms at the prefill dispatcher. Code at https://github.com/sudokara/Kairos.

evidence.claim: Prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT across the five workloads; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait plus inter-node KV-cache transfer (e.g., Bursty: 840.8 ms prefill queue, 1,070.1 ms prefill exec, 2,175.6 ms KV transfer, 7,893.9 ms end-to-end P95).
evidence.baseline: Canonical 2P2D disaggregated serving (2 prefill + 2 decode nodes), no deflection
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.1 Claim 2 and Table 3, PDF Pages 4-5

evidence.claim: Kairos reduces P95 TTFT by up to 81% and raises SLO attainment by up to 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers, at sub-millisecond per-request routing cost.
evidence.value: up to 81% P95 TTFT reduction; up to 79% higher SLO attainment; <1 ms routing
evidence.condition: Production-derived trace (Company X); bursty load; 2P2D A100 cluster; DeepSeek-V2-Lite; vLLM 0.18.1
evidence.source_locator: Abstract and Section 1 Contributions, PDF Pages 1-2

evidence.claim: Utilization is complementary: prefill SM utilization is 75-84% while decode SM utilization never exceeds 27%; the gap is widest in HPLD (84% prefill vs 7.5% decode), confirming decode-side compute slack available for chunked prefill.
evidence.condition: Five workloads; A100 80GB; measured via NVIDIA Nsight Systems
evidence.source_locator: Section 3 Claim 1 and Table 2, PDF Pages 3-4

evidence.claim: Injecting chunked prefill into decode batches keeps decode step-latency increase within 30 ms for chunk sizes up to 512 tokens across all workloads and batch sizes; for chunk sizes >= 1024 the first-chunk increase reaches about 30 ms (low-prefill regimes) up to about 50 ms (bursty/high-prefill regimes), so using large first chunks requires knowledge of cached-token volume.
evidence.value: delta T_step <= 30 ms for chunk size <= 512; up to ~50 ms for >= 1024
evidence.baseline: Decode step latency with no chunked-prefill injection
evidence.condition: Mixed prefill-decode batches on decode nodes across the five workloads

evidence.claim: Deflected requests execute prefill in place on the decode node, eliminating the inter-node KV-cache transfer; the system needs only one-time deployment-time profiling, no model changes, and imposes less than 1 ms per-request scheduling overhead (~2000 lines of Python on vLLM 0.18.1).
evidence.value: inter-node KV transfer eliminated for deflected requests; <1 ms routing; ~2000 LoC
evidence.baseline: Canonical disaggregated serving ships KV cache from prefill node to decode node
evidence.condition: Kairos on vLLM 0.18.1; 2P2D A100; deflected requests only
evidence.source_locator: Sections 1-2 Contributions and Design, PDF Pages 1-2

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Cluster: 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), each an NVIDIA A100 80GB; the paper also compared 2P2D against 1P3D and 3P1D on the Bursty workload (1P3D saturates the single prefill node with median prefill queue >2x of 2P2D; 3P1D is capacity-limited on the single decode node, where KV-cache occupancy forces transfer back-pressure and inflates end-to-end TTFT). Traces are derived from a large-scale production LLM serving deployment (Company X), replayed against DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MoE); token counts normalized to its 32K context window preserving prompt-to-completion ratio (prompt P25/median/P90 = 2,071/3,569/10,336; completion 21/50/163; median prefill-to-decode ratio 69.7, well above NVIDIA Dynamo's 8:1 disaggregation threshold with RDMA). Five workloads (Table 1): LPLD (RPS 22, P:D 61.46), LPHD (RPS 20, P:D 4.99), HPLD (RPS 1, P:D 1482.89), HPHD (RPS 1, P:D 66.53), and Bursty (RPS 4, P:D 69.67, Gamma inter-arrival from long-tailed production distribution). SLO targets: 4 s P95 TTFT, 70 ms TBT. Implementation on vLLM 0.18.1 (~2000 LoC Python), <1 ms per-request routing. Baselines: state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers; throughput compared against PD disaggregation in Figure 5 (Kairos comparable or higher, holding to 7 RPS per the partially visible Page 10 text).
previous_facts.limitations: The headline 'up to 81% TTFT / 79% SLO attainment' are best-case, bursty-load figures from the abstract/contributions; the precise baseline identities and per-workload, per-RPS conditions are in the not-yet-visible Section 6, and at lower request rates Kairos behaves similarly to standard PD disaggregation (little gain). Evaluated on a single small cluster (2P2D, four A100s) and a single model architecture (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, MoE); larger pools and other architectures are not shown in the visible evidence. Benefit depends on decode-side compute slack and workload regime, and using chunk size >= 1024 for the first chunk requires cached-token-volume awareness. The visible evidence reports GPU SM/TC/HBM utilization but not aggregate KV-cache bytes transferred or network-bandwidth utilization as outcome metrics.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to the TPN/KV-transfer topic: Kairos is a per-request, KV-cache-occupancy-aware scheduler that eliminates inter-node KV-cache transfer for deflected requests by running prefill in place on decode nodes, and it reports end-to-end P95 TTFT (up to 81% lower) and SLO attainment, which the topic values. Important boundary for project inference: Kairos is a GPU-pool/scheduling-side mechanism, not a network-side optimization; it avoids KV transfer rather than making the network faster, so it illustrates what scheduling alone can achieve and does not answer the topic's question about the irreplaceable value of network-side mechanisms. The visible evidence does not report network utilization, KV-transfer bytes, or TPOT as improved outcome metrics.
source_notes: Primary arXiv PDF (2607.02043v1) fetched; evidence covers abstract, intro/design (Pages 1-2), empirical study with Tables 1-3 and Figure 1 (Pages 3-5), and a partial throughput result (Page 10).
System is named Kairos in the body; the abstract describes it as a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler.
The 81%/79% headline figures are abstract/contribution claims; their exact baseline and per-workload conditions are recorded as a gap pending the unread Section 6.
